attributes.context: Paragraph 4 of the NEW TECHNOLOGY letter states that the committee is made up of the Vice President of Human Resources and the Director of Quality Assurance and is chaired by the Vice President of Operations.

extraction_text: Quarterly meetings will be held with the Union Senior Negotiating Committee to acquaint them with substantive developments in this area, including timely advice to the Union regarding Company plans to introduce new technology as defined in paragraph 2 above.

attributes.context: This is the final paragraph of the NEW TECHNOLOGY letter, following the definition of new technology and the retraining and committee provisions.

extraction_text: Any new job classifications created as the result of technological changes will be reviewed in advance with the Union.

attributes.context: The extraction appears in a DUAL MACHINE TOOL OPERATION letter that confirms the parties’ understanding regarding assignment and payment of employees who operate more than one machine tool concurrently.

extraction_text: It is understood that the scope of this agreement extends to assignments on specialized machine tools in four categories, i.e., tape controlled (except Skin Mills), console operated, computer controlled, and semi-automatic machine tools (except Rivet Headers and Saw Sharpeners). The agreement does not include conventional machine tools, and employees will not be assigned to operate more than one conventional machine tool concurrently. No employee will be required to operate concurrently more than two specialized machine tools as described above.

attributes.context: Paragraph 2 defines “new technology” as automated machines, robots, and computer-aided systems that eliminate manually performed hourly work; paragraph 4 sets committee members and quarterly Union meetings.

extraction_text: In recognition of the Union's expressed concerns, the Company will establish a committee which will deal with the introduction of new machinery and equipment with the goal of assuring that the employees, whose jobs are directly eliminated by the introduction of new machinery and equipment, will be offered retraining in the event that equivalent job opportunities are not available. Normally, this training will be accomplished on the employee's own time and is intended to provide equal or better job opportunities than would have existed had the new machinery or equipment installation not occurred. Such training will only be for a job for which the Company foresees a requirement.

attributes.context: This is paragraph 3 of the 2002-31 letter titled NEW TECHNOLOGY. Paragraph 2 defines new technology as automated manufacturing machines, robots, and computer-aided manufacturing systems that directly eliminate work performed manually by hourly-represented employees.
This follows paragraph 3 of the 2002-31 NEW TECHNOLOGY letter, which establishes a committee to deal with new machinery and equipment and provide retraining, and paragraph 2 defines new technology.
This is the final provision in the 2002-31 NEW TECHNOLOGY letter, which also defines new technology in paragraph 2 and establishes committee and retraining procedures for new machinery and equipment.
